newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi stocks gain on hopes of Chidambaram's return. [CORRECTED 14:06 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Delhi stocks gain on hopes of Chidambaram's return. [CORRECTED 14:06 GMT]

text.p: Delhi share prices closed higher on Monday as investors bought on hopes that former finance minister P. Chidambaram's Tamil Maanila Congress (TMC) party might join the government, brokers said.
The Delhi Stock Exchange's sensitive index ended 2.67 (corrects from 8.49) points higher at 800.34 (corrects from 806.16) points.

"Share prices have been rising on buying by investors on expectations that TMC would join the government, which would give more stability to the recently formed coalition government," said Bharat Bhushan of brokers Nu-Era Equity.
The Tamil Maanila Congress (TMC) on Sunday authorised its leader, G.K. Moopanar, to decide whether the regional party should join India's new government.

The TMC, part of the centre-left United Front coalition, decided on April 19 to stay out of the government after the alliance chose Inder Kumar Gujral instead of Moopanar as its leader and new prime minister.
The TMC's decision was keenly awaited by investors because Chidambaram is a key economic reformer who presented a tax-cutting budget for 1997/98 (April-March) on February 28.
"If Chidambaram comes back as the country's finance minister, the market should witness another bull-run," said another broker.
Gujral has not appointed a finance minister in his cabinet, signalling the slot was open for Chidambaram. The budget has yet to win parliamentary approval.
Traders said foreign institutional investors and domestic mutual funds mopped up shares of select blue-chip companies and aided the upward movement in share prices.
Reliance Industries rose 6.40 rupees to 304.40 on steady buying by speculators and foreign investors as the share entered a no-delivery period for the next one month, brokers said.
ACC quoted 41.75 rupees higher at 1,476.75 on speculative buying, they said.
However State Bank of India ended 1.25 rupees lower at 316.45 on late selling by speculators.
